reviews.text: 一开始有点意思，慢慢的就感觉有点无聊了，不过整体还行吧
第一把80亿身材，果然我玩demo的时候想的阵容还是牛批的，懒说配听，跟我的大运说去吧，我们都在用力的活着！！！
啊
初步体验了下，流派非常的多，随机性非常的强，不过感觉经验值获取的速度没想象中的快
游戏本身问题还是相当多的，距离那些优质的肉鸽差的很远，但在我这里达到及格标准了，主要玩法这一块真的加大分 如果不打无尽模式并且带一点点SL的话，游戏体验还是不错的，至少值回了这个价格。反正我玩得挺开心的
关注这游戏蛮久的，平衡性一直是自走棋游戏比较难攻克的问题，好在作者还是听劝的，陆陆续续都有在更新。初体验感觉入门简单，关卡的难度是循序渐进的，想通关的话还是有点考验玩家对游戏机制的理解。
感觉游戏的难度是有的，但是建构深度也是很大的，刚开始上手玩到时候，经常死的莫名其妙，直到玩明白之后，把把都是爽局
游戏趣味性还是可以的，上手难度虽然有些高，需要时间去摸索各种卡的联动，有了理解后面就有好的爽感，问题是到了后面内容有些同质化，卡池浅，敌人种类也少，需要多多更新增加内容才行
很喜欢游戏的美术风格，角色的动态效果很棒，攻击特效很爽，游玩体验很不错～
游戏的趣味性丰富多彩。金色战士的池子明显还未完全建立健全，估计后续会增加。

The criticisms about grind and lack of content are valid, but the game still serves up a pretty strong package. I got this on the cheap in a bundle, so I don't feel as sour about its shortcomings. That said, I understood what this game was going for, and your reward for reading this is my recommending two indie autobattlers that do it better: Underboard and Million Monster Militia.

I really don't understand the mixed reviews on this one. It's an excellent little autobattler. Nice presentation, easy to put together synergies, nice difficulty curve. The only major problem I have with it is that there aren't many units so runs tend to turn out pretty similar after a while and difficulty taps out a little too quickly. Be aware if you want to 100% the game, it's a lot of grinding. I'm at 75% with 24 hours and it'd be about 2-3x that much time to grind out the rest of the achievements. And there really isn't enough variation to sustain interest for that long. Overall tho, solid and definitely enjoyed my time with it. 7/10
Nice auto battler with its downsides, but more than great for the asking price

It's a good game but keep in mind the amount of content is VERY small especially since it forces you to grind a lot. It's well designed and runs well and is fun... for a while but it is badly in need of more content/units especially. At the bare minimum better ways to get units you want/remove the chance of getting units you don't but mostly it just needs more actual units and frankly a even though there are few units theres STILL some that are absolutely worthless/a gold trap.

Fun game. Great presentation, great UI, high quality all around - legendary even for this genre. Challenging until you get the gist and some unlocks rolling. Can be beaten with a variety of builds along the way that spices things up. There's nothing rocket science here but still plenty of systems to chew on. I'm usually pretty casual but I was inspired by this game to beat it on every difficulty, with every character, and unlocked every trinket thus unlocking everything. The game beat me up a little early and revenge was thoroughly handled. The power of auto battling compelled me. And I'm still playing even though there's nothing left to unlock. Beating the game mercilessly in different ways with the plethora of trinkets to entertain myself and attempting to push endless further. There's enough bang for buck here but since I've seen and done it all about the only negative I can posit is the obligatory "I wish there was more content" but that's just because one hates to see a good time come to an end, especially in this grossly underserved genre.

Knightica is a fantasy strategy roguelike developed by Mad Mango Games and published by Goblinz Publishing and WR game that blends auto-battler mechanics, tactical positioning, and roguelike progression into a surprisingly deep and addictive experience. While the concept initially appears simple, the game quickly reveals a strong focus on planning, army synergy, and strategic adaptation that gives every run a satisfying sense of progression. By combining accessible mechanics with meaningful tactical decisions, Knightica manages to feel approachable for newcomers while still offering enough complexity to keep strategy fans engaged for hours. The game places players in command of a growing warband tasked with reclaiming lands overrun by dark forces and monstrous enemies. Instead of controlling units directly during combat, players prepare for battle beforehand by recruiting soldiers, arranging formations, applying upgrades, and building synergies between different units and abilities. Once combat begins, battles unfold automatically, meaning success depends almost entirely on preparation and smart decision-making rather than reflexes. This structure transforms even small tactical choices into important factors that can completely determine the outcome of difficult encounters. One of the game’s strongest qualities is how rewarding experimentation feels. Every run introduces randomized opportunities that encourage players to adapt their strategies rather than rely on a single repetitive build. Some runs may focus on defensive formations supported by healing and armor upgrades, while others reward aggressive offensive setups capable of eliminating enemies before they can respond. Discovering powerful combinations between units, enchantments, and relic-style bonuses becomes one of the most enjoyable parts of the experience. The game constantly encourages players to test new ideas and refine strategies through repeated attempts. Positioning also plays a surprisingly important role despite the automatic combat system. Unit placement before battles can dramatically affect survivability and overall effectiveness, especially during later stages where enemies become significantly more dangerous. Frontline placement, ranged support, ability timing, and formation balance all contribute to victory or defeat. Because combat itself cannot be directly controlled once it begins, every preparation phase carries meaningful tension as players attempt to predict how battles will unfold. The progression systems are particularly satisfying because upgrades consistently feel impactful. Units can evolve into stronger versions, receive powerful enchantments, and gain abilities that fundamentally alter how the army performs in battle. Certain combinations can create devastating chain reactions capable of destroying entire enemy formations, while others focus on survivability or long-term scaling. The constant flow of upgrades gives every run a strong sense of momentum, rewarding players with noticeable increases in power as they progress deeper into the game. The roguelike structure greatly enhances replayability. Since enemy encounters, upgrades, and progression paths are randomized, no two runs feel exactly the same. Even failed attempts usually provide useful experience that helps players understand stronger combinations or more efficient strategies for future runs. This gradual mastery becomes one of the game’s most addictive qualities because improvement feels tied to both player knowledge and in-run progression systems. Visually, Knightica uses a colorful fantasy art style that prioritizes readability and charm. Unit designs are distinct and expressive, making it easy to identify abilities and battlefield roles during combat. The environments and interface remain clean and easy to navigate, helping the game avoid unnecessary visual clutter despite the large number of units and effects appearing on screen during later battles. Animations are smooth and satisfying, giving combat enough energy to remain entertaining even though the fights themselves are automated. The soundtrack complements the fantasy setting effectively without becoming repetitive during extended play sessions. Music helps maintain a sense of adventure and tension while allowing players to remain focused on strategy and planning. Sound effects also provide satisfying feedback for attacks, upgrades, and major ability activations, making successful builds feel impactful and rewarding to watch unfold. Another impressive aspect of Knightica is how well it balances accessibility with strategic depth. New players can quickly understand the basic gameplay loop, but mastering the game requires learning how units interact, how positioning affects combat, and which upgrade paths provide the strongest long-term benefits. This layered complexity gives the game a satisfying learning curve that steadily rewards players who invest time into understanding its systems. However, the game is not without shortcomings. Because combat resolves automatically after preparation, some players may eventually wish for more direct control during battles. Randomness also plays a major role in progression, and certain runs can feel heavily dependent on receiving favorable upgrades or strong unit combinations early enough to survive tougher encounters. While replayability is high, repeated runs may occasionally begin to feel structurally similar once players become familiar with the available enemy types and progression systems. The game’s roguelike nature may also frustrate players who dislike repeated failures and gradual mastery-based progression. Advancement often requires experimentation, adaptation, and learning from unsuccessful runs rather than immediate success. Additionally, while the fantasy setting is charming, the game places far greater emphasis on gameplay systems than on storytelling or world-building, which may leave narrative-focused players wanting more. Despite these limitations, Knightica succeeds remarkably well at creating a satisfying tactical gameplay loop built around strategy and experimentation. Every successful run feels earned through smart preparation and synergy building rather than simple luck alone. The game consistently rewards players who carefully study its systems and adapt their strategies based on changing circumstances. Knightica ultimately stands out as a polished and highly replayable roguelike strategy game that combines auto-battler mechanics with rewarding tactical depth. Its addictive progression systems, satisfying customization options, and strong emphasis on strategic planning create an experience that remains engaging across repeated runs. While the reliance on automated combat and random upgrades may not appeal to everyone, fans of strategy roguelikes and synergy-driven gameplay will likely find Knightica to be an extremely enjoyable and cleverly designed fantasy experience. Rating: 7/10
Much deeper than some of the comments are giving it credit for. Well done.
This game is a super fun merge and auto-battler! It's simple yet has depth and has given me hours of fun when I need something relaxing to play.
It is cute... but not that deep...

好像有很多流派，最后其实只有9个公主加1到2个旷工做工具人然后配合找干锅+国王或者机甲直接抽干的组合……R了几个小时终于到25了，然后就可以卸载了
对不起这个价格，我首发就入了，除了一个英雄没解锁之外打了好几个英雄的三星难度，打到后期都是重复的阵容重复的套路，附魔有用的太少，强的就几个，今天好久没打了，下一个重新玩玩，发现游戏都进不去，点启动会直接卡死，体验非常之差，不建议入。
无尽第二十四关没人能过，我几百万亿的数值boss根本不掉血 数值过百亿就开始显示？？？？ 二十四关boss直接无敌 逆天

绝对不推荐。 1. 极其无聊的数值游戏。——一切的原罪 你的数值够大就可以为所欲为，在无尽的第13波，我的随从的攻防来到了40位数，显示为？？？？，是的你可以清楚的看到有一个成就就是达成？？？？。 2. 崩坏的数值，糟糕的平衡。 参考第一点，在指数增强的随从面前，大部分的设计就显得极其可笑和无聊，尤其高难度下很多附魔/法术/随从就是纯粹的垃圾。 3. 可笑的对战。 参考第一点，在数值面前，毫不关心对战。 4. 吝啬的精英怪奖励 ≈一个几元的法术 5. 崩坏的UI 在？？？？之前，随从的属性有39位数， 众所周知8个0是亿，这是多少亿我已经说不清了，然而我要顶着这么长的数字去玩，我完全分不清我的随从之间的大小，以及和对手之间随从的大小，你完全不知道自己在玩什么。 6. 负面＞正面的“奖励” 大部分奖励的负面效果远大于正面效果，不得不说这也是游戏设计的特色了吧，策划会玩游戏吗？你自己用你设计出来的垃圾给我通一个看看？ 7. 意义不明的对战 参考1、3点，在我的机器人比对面大10倍的情况下，打不过一个数值上小10倍的高频率怪，这种完全看不明白对战计算的方式，让人不得不怀疑部分随从的属性就是比别人更不值钱，而且你完全不知道谁的更值钱。 当然，这一点不能算是缺点，毕竟谁让你的属性只比对面大10倍呢？ 懒得喷了，这篇评论是我对这个游戏最后的耐心，之前有多期待，现在就有多失望。

数值拿脚填的？对手成长曲线认真的吗？每回合给十块钱，没利息，一个地块要尼玛六块，图鉴也没有拿了才知道夯还是屎，攻击方式也只写远近不写范围单体，作为肉鸽广受好评的局外成长是没有的，我想玩别的职业解锁条件更是恶心。还有那逼竞技场，对面明显经济实力高于当前水平，就一次运气好打了九胜，绝大部分对局都死在四五胜，既然是指挥官对决你能不能吧对面设成同等胜场同等经济的对手？最难绷的一把四回合我一堆白绿卡打对面蓝紫卡真是给自己气笑了 补：靠着开局roll巨魔也是过了困难，然后就不得不提尼玛的傻逼无尽模式，第一波BOSS尼玛5000攻8000防是尼玛人能想出来的数值？ 再补：战士极难过了，全靠开局ROLL紫卡+ 2-1神抽金卡，这逼游戏没点运气是真玩不了，突然就暴毙了，紫金卡明明后期才能拿，给的属性抠抠搜搜来得晚根本没一点用。 总之游戏是有意思的，就是玩得吭吃瘪肚很无语，看后续更新能不能改得更好，至少普通难度得让我爽吧？啥时候玩爽了啥时候改好评 最后补一下，玩了也有两天了，竞技场极难无尽都过了，但是最后一个角色解锁解锁进度五分之四，你就玩吧，一玩一个不吱声

挺可惜的一款游戏，是的，我想说的是很可惜。这个游戏框架是好的，各种要素融合的也多，本应该成为一款自由度很高的游戏的，但不得不说填充的东西太少了，以至于我怀疑这个游戏的作者既没有仔细研究过自走棋，也没认真玩过杀戮尖塔这种rouge游戏，或者说我怀疑作者可能并不怎么喜欢玩这两种类型的游戏。 这游戏所有的流派其实都是一个流派，那就是堆数值，前期加的少，后期加的巨多。每个章节思考的都是怎么混过这关，根本不需要考虑后面的成长，因为下一章节的数值一定比你这章节给的多，甚至不同流派成长曲线都是一模一样的。 rouge类游戏和自走棋类游戏本应该给人不断的即时奖励刺激，每一步都是迈向体系大成的一步，甚至偶尔会迈出一大步，让玩家欣喜若狂，在体系大成无敌的一刻，享受多巴胺轰炸的感觉。但这个游戏给我的体验就像在玩没有剧情的角色扮演游戏一样，目标只有肉眼可见的升级和数值，我甚至觉得贵作者之前是做换皮手游的。

美术是真的不错，从demo开始就一直期待正式版，但是实际上手体验之后非常失望，起码这个版本来说远不是一个成熟完善的版本，不推荐购买。 主要缺点： 一、流程过短 本以为试玩的两个章节只是开始，没想到正式版居然一共只有三个章节，我的体感是好不容易胡了一把结果刚发育起来还没开始爽就结束了，虽说有无尽模式但是数值填的过于离谱，能轻松打过最终boss的阵容在无尽里撑不过三关就没了，经常是好不容易开满了格子养起了大哥就得下一把再见了，一点都没有肉鸽游戏胡起来的爽感。 二、奖励太少 游戏里的精英怪数值本来就很变态，超出普通怪物太多，结果辛辛苦苦打完后的奖励跟蚊子肉一样，你去就要承担暴毙的风险，但是打完收益就仅仅是强化下次刷新，也就是说脸黑的情况下一次没刷到需要的东西就等于空过，那不去行不行呢？更不行，因为其他房间更差劲，卵用没有的酒馆除了加血就只有+50exp，完全是浪费特殊房间次数，稍微好用点的随从房和法术房也要大量的金币才能消费，但是最逆天的是想攒金币除了拿矿工以外就真的只能10块钱10块钱的攒，利息这种最基础的东西居然是打过boss才能概率刷出来的天赋，再加上本身开格子就要花很多钱，不走贪婪真的会穷到进不起随从房和法术房只能去精英怪赌脸。 三、ui混乱 这游戏单位的ui应该是我见过自走棋品类下最差的，该写清的一概不写，老老实实写清楚血量攻击防御技能buff不香吗？有的单位是群攻面板看不出来，有的单位同样是远程只能打一个，有的单位死了人攻击就会下降但是具体什么关系也不知道，有的单位会奶人面板根本没有体现，就在介绍里轻描淡写了一句，我是看技能特效才发现的，但是根本不说到底奶多少血，我也根本不知道奶那些多人队伍到底是怎么结算的，还有类似国王这样的传奇单位，我只能从特效上分辨好像在普攻以外有一招aoe，最绷不住的是“雇佣兵”这个棋子，中文描述“将剩余金币转化伤害”，你加个转化我就一直以为是要扣钱所以从没拿过，直到后期全是贪婪才想拿一个试试结果发现根本就不扣钱，你描述成“获得金币数量xx%的伤害”不就没有这个歧义了吗？ 四、没有图鉴 很难想象这种类型的游戏居然没有图鉴，当然按照现在的尿性就算有图鉴也是那种狗屎ui推起来的图鉴，但是起码有图鉴你能让刚接触的人找找思路吧，连图鉴都没有就敢号称正式版拿出来卖，这个圈钱的态度是真的不行。 五、棋子太少 越是稀有的棋子品类越少，很多种族根本就没有传奇，我以为是自己脸黑，但是玩了一晚上还是那几个就说明问题了。 六、逆天操作 看评论区才想起来少吐槽一点，就是调整站位的操作，你这游戏好歹也是跟背包乱斗一个包卖的就不能学学人家吗？智障一样的操作，必须把手里的东西放下才能调整下面的棋子，策划要不你花三十块钱买一个玩玩吧，背包管理游戏调站位难受是真的不想玩了。 总结： 好消息：demo体量不小 坏消息：正式版体量也就这样，只能说期望越大失望越大吧，作品根本没有打磨就当正式版发售的制作组估计也没那个耐心继续完善，跑路的可能性不小，总之喜欢美术的可以先玩玩demo观望一下，正式版谨慎购入
饰品升级太慢了，就算打完也不过才升一级。这本来就是休闲玩乐的小游戏，结果却要花大量时间重复游玩提升等级解锁饰品，不话时间就无法体验全部内容，本末倒置了。设计团队想延长游玩时间应该更注重游戏的内容，让玩家自己愿意反复游玩，而不是搞个等级解锁饰品，逼玩家刷等级，不然部分饰品不给用，这样只会让玩家反感。

由于游戏美术风格自洽，机制优雅简洁，demo期间就玩了很久，但是正式版发售之后比较失望，感觉游戏在某些地方做的减法是不是过多了 1.有些时候养成过难，有些时候又过于简单，而且非常看脸，极端情况下开局刷个巨魔或者萨满，那这一局就是躺着也能过了。比如说贪婪系几乎就是无脑强，不管是绿色的废品回收工（获得金币+1数值），还是蓝色的雇佣兵（金币转化为数值)，都在前期就有很强的自养成能力，更不要说还有矿工这个最强经济卡加持；骑士系的枪兵弓兵不仅格子大占地方，而且都是临时加成，直到军士出现才能给他一点蚊子腿加成，极难难度下就是前期抽到三四个军士都是慢性死亡；奥术师系的养成手公主更是要到史诗才出现，前期的主要战力来源就是自己掏钱买法师叠上去，至于巫师玩过的都知道那个经验涨的有多慢多坐牢 2.由于棋子机制是隐式的，没有写在描述里，导致攻防数值对战力的影响很不直观，尤其是少人单位的作战能力比群体单位高贵了非常多。比如说巫师和法师同属奥术师流派，法师的攻击是aoe，攻击力比率似乎也比巫师高，加上单位数量比巫师要少，导致大部分情况下即使是同等攻防法师也完爆巫师，战斗力大约是巫师的三倍以上，同样的情况还发生在骑士流派的军士和枪兵里，每次看到数值两三倍于军士的枪兵在对方的aoe之下死死伤伤，军士单兵冲锋陷阵就觉得很好笑，三个敌方boss就不用说了，攻防就是用脚填的，纯粹是想写多少写多少，以他们的实际战斗表现来看除以十差不多 3.制作组是不是过高的估计了刷新的价值？精英怪的奖励几乎全是一次性的，同时还有大量的负面效果，经常出现打完精英怪三个恶魔宝藏一点用都没有，对战斗力零提升的情况出现，我印象里那种全局生效的机制类buff只会在打完大boss才出现，这方面在别的游戏里都是乐趣的重要来源，这里给得太吝啬了 4.附魔的机制让人迷惑，我现在也没搞清楚那些冰箭、闪电、爆弹助手实际能让一个主攻手的输出能力提升多少，感觉输出能力多到一定程度之后只是在污染我的附魔池，几个关键的附魔比如学习达人、自私自利经常刷了几十轮都刷不到手上

Все же поставлю минус. Приятный игровой процесс но на этом все. Мало контента в игре, механики не такие интересные, и как будто не доделанные чтоли. расстановка юнитов по столу должна решать но все боссы или минибоссы или умеют телепортироваться по всему столу или спаунить врагов где угодно. [h2]I wish I could give this game a thumbs sideways.[/h2] [h3]Let's start with being nice[/h3] This is a nice game. It has a very cute art style with simple troop combat. The exp system is more fun than the standard merge three then merge three of the merge. The thing that makes auto-battler style games truly fun to ME is when the game provides you with pieces to a combo but never the full thing so you make due with interesting cross-type synergy. [u]"I got this succubus who steals defense but I don't have any of the other unholy troops that synergize with her, but I [i]could[/i] use my big tanky guys from a completely different class and use their self-defense buffs to drain back into her."[/u] This game does have that. This game gives you a lot of random pieces and the spells are extremely extremely random and cannot be forced at all. So in a very simple way, this game provides a fun experience which can be worth it to you, but only if you really like this genre already. [h3]Now I vent[/h3] This game has a very distinct lack of content. There being only 1 arcanist at the lowest tier is depressing. I mean yeah these games are like, you're not supposed to build from the very start of the game and be like "Yup, this is my build forever" but it's like, at least some variety would be nice. I hate getting up a build using all the cool mechs and knowing in advance there is literally no capstone mecha at legendary for the build, I'm basically just relying on spamming as many of the Mecha as possible. Only to lose, because it of course sucks and doesn't have a capstone, hudoy. I don't think it matters at all what you make as your build in the first two areas, as long as they can beat the bosses. On the higher difficulties (I couldn't beat insane just saying that now) I would eventually just skip every single elite combat because I never had a build that would tempo out strong enough to actually beat them. Losing to a boss loses the whole run so that's more important. Speaking of bosses, there are only 3. The spider queen, the tentacle lord, and then big spooky sorcerer. These fights do not change per run, except in extremely minor ways if even. They are honestly quite easy for the most part, as I guess the devs were scared of doing something similar to other roguelikes where bosses end up being choke-points in runs, where here you are literally guaranteed in what you get so there's no possible way to ever get countered by them except by their overly inflated stats to an insane degree. Sure, I guess sometimes it does feel bad when you got an ultimate shiv combo in Slay the Spire and get matched against the Time Lord who automatically counters you, but I mean when that fight shows up you can account and plan around it for the rest of the area, and it wouldn't be as fun if the boss was just a pushover. Also that game came out 7 years ago and each area had 3 bosses, and this game has literally only one boss. But yeah in order to make up for that kind of difficulty, they just made the bosses here beyond simple so basically every build can beat them... but their stats are extremely overly inflated. It gets quite hard on hard but in impossible it feels like incline uphill higher and higher then wall, scale this vertical cliffside or fall and die. Ugh. Enemy variety too. Enemies are very simple, but you fight the same ones over and over. The only ones that are entirely optional are elites, and even then you will see their non-elite versions basically guaranteed. [h3]My own personal example of the run that made me just give up.[/h3] So I had one run where I got mercenaries pretty early, and I really liked the idea of having hybrid tank + damage dealers. The game gave me a pointer that I could use multiple instead of stacking all the levels into one and thus I did so. Then I also got succubus and was using her + the constantly boosting mercenaries to keep them tanking up while being drained for her own ability to solo-carry. It felt really fun. Then, I found princess. Then I found princess. Then I found spellblade and dark lord. I wanted to keep my original board but like, idk I'm not just gonna ignore the game giving me the crazy good stuff. By the end of the run, looking at the stats, my stack of mercenaries and succubus that I have been building up for the entire game since area 1 managed to do, I kid you not, less than [b]5% of my army's total damage and tanking. BOTH.[/b] None of what I did with them mattered in the slightest, all that mattered was I got a princess stack leveling each other up and leveling up everyone else and leveling up like crazy making the spellblade and dark lord repeatedly eating the spellblade way stronger than anything I have ever done. I literally could've sold everything the instant I got to the third area and I'm pretty sure I still would've just won anyway. [b]Let me be entirely honest here![/b] The game being simple is not actually a problem. The lack of content is really the thing that makes it feel like, is this game REALLY worth 15+ dollars? Something I intentionally neglected to mention until the end is that there is actually a large amount of recolored sprites in this game. You might've been able to guess when I brought up that elites have regular versions you fight in normal encounters. One of the elites is straight up slapped as an ally troop but green. With so many recolors, I am shocked with how little choice there is in build variety in the game. If you like a simple auto battler and don't care about the lack of variety and content per run, then this game may in fact be fun for you. This is actually the reason why I wanted to give it a completely medium review instead of negative. While I had a negative time with it, and I don't believe most people would like a game wide as an ocean deep as a puddle, it has makings of a quality experience and it could be fun for people actually passionate about the game. I wouldn't recommend it for most people, it'd just be completely mid for them. You should only give this game if my negative examples here literally do not matter to you, because then of course it's just all positives!

[h2]Great Concept // Cute Art // Incomplete Game [/h2] Knightica (much like many other games being released these days) suffers from launching before the game is done. It's using customers as an open beta instead of having the game ready at launch. It's a fun enough autobattler with a spacial puzzle thrown in for good measure. There is a lot to like here. The art is cute and well done, the game pacing is solid, and there are great ideas that just aren't implemented well enough to make a good game. It's entertaining and even though over half of my play time is leaving the game on overnight, I have played enough that I probably got my money's worth. I wouldn't recommend it to anyone [b]yet[/b], but I expect the devs (who have been active) to get it right as they continue to work on it. You can see a lot of love went into this, and I did enjoy playing it. [h3]Biggest issues: [/h3] [b]1. An inability to trust the UI:[/b] Easily the biggest issue, even prior to lag every ~15-30 minutes or so the game will glitch and you will grab (or not grab) a unit you meant to and it might result in a minor inconvenience or a run ending mistake (oops I just sold the unit I spent 20 turns building up and is 90% of my army strength). I watched this happen to a streamer and though, ahh, it wasn't the game you just weren't paying attention, but after it happened to me for the 3rd time while I was focused I understood the frustration. Unless you want to pause after every unit pickup to confirm it is in fact picked up, be prepared to have some random (potentially run ending) handicaps thrown in. [b]2. Opaque / Misleading Information:[/b] This is the biggest problem with the game. Units don't do what you expect them to. There is no clear indication of what Attack or Defense do or mean. Damage / Health tracking are unreliable. On that note, it's unclear what units have AOE, or any other feature. I even had 2 identical ranged units placed side by side, one with 300 attack and one with 150 attack. The one with 150 attack out damaged the 300 attack unit. I don't know why, and there was no indication why. This is like having a tower defense game where instead of providing damage, attack speed, and AOE size as stats they had a "general strength" stat. Occasionally a unit will tell you it has AOE or hint at it in the description, but there's no way to know how big the AOE is (which varries greatly as far as I can tell). Some units take way more hits than others. If I buff a ranged units defense to 2k it will die faster than certain tanky looking units with 1k defense. Other tanky looking units die really fast. There needs to be more and better information provided. [h3]Other Notable Issues:[/h3] [b]1. Memory Leaks[/b]: that get worse as you play. By the end of run 2 (and yes the game is good enough that I wanted to play twice in a row) I couldn't select my units consistently unless I paused on each pick up. The lag is real, and it makes playing awful. Restarting solves the issue, but I shouldn't need to restart every 2 hours to play a game. [b]2. Lack of Variety/Unifinished End Game:[/b] There is no endgame except an endless mode which is really a "how big do I want to get before I quit" game if you're scaling fast enough. Not my cup of tea, but it was nice to keep playing some runs that were going well for a little bit. The game is the same 3 bosses every run, no variation, and there's some small amount of strategy to them, but it's mostly did I get generically strong enough. I'm pretty sure the enemy army comps are the same every time, but it doesn't really matter that much because it's much more about your comp then theirs. In campaign mode, if you beat the 2nd boss you should always win the run unless you make a big mistake. Arena didn't feel particularly challenging or interesting, but hopefully they'll keep adding new comps to that. There is no PvP. [b]3. No Undo:[/b] Some of the other issues might be less annoying if there was an undo button, but in a game where you can accidentally sell off the bulk of army strength with one misclick (or game glitch), or get your board stuck so that you can't put a unit back on the field without selling what you just bought... well it's frustrating. Undo would be extremely welcome. [h3]The Good:[/h3] After all that I do like this game, and I hope they get it working well. If they do resolve the major issues it would be a lot of fun to play. The art is wonderful. The game flow is solid. The ideas are great even if everything isn't balanced particularly well. The spacial puzzle is fun (although it can be frustrating with no undo option). Unit selection is fun. Building a comp is fun. It all adds up to a game that is... almost fun enough, but maybe too frustrating? It's something I want to want to keep playing, but the problems stop me. It was fun enough to play for 40 hours, so if that's what you're looking for maybe go for it. I wish I had waited a few months, but maybe I'll enjoy it again after a few patches. The devs already added an option to keep your shop locked after combat (which was sorely needed) and rebalanced a few things (maybe a bit too far), so there's hope that this will get better. I look forward to playing again once unit info is more transparent and there are more interesting boss fights.

Look, the game does most things well, but the one thing is does poorly is literally enough to ruin the entire thing. The units stats lie to you in a game about optimizing unit stats. The devs decided to use a hidden strength multiplier for unit power levels which acts on the visible power number - so you can have 2 different units each with 10 power, but one will do significantly more or less than the other. Their solution? "Oh, we made the codex [in-game encyclopedia] which lists all units and monsters so you can see the hidden stat!" ... Oh, great, cool, okay, so I [b]have to open the codex, multiply my unit's current 'power' by its hidden 'strength' value, divide it by the number of character models in the unit, and then do that process again for whatever I'm trying to compare them against[/b]? You compare unit stats [i]CONSTANTLY[/i] in this game and THAT'S your solution?? Honestly unplayable and I wish I could get a refund, because this is SUCH an easy fix. You don't need new art, and the math is dead simple. Put a toggle in the options to show EITHER the raw value OR the calculated value. That's it. The game's been out for over 6 months and yet they chose to make a whole "codex" instead of something they could have hotfixed overnight. It reeks of stubbornness or "chatGPT wrote my game and I don't know how to fix it", which, either way, is a terrible look, so no, I don't recommend this even if it's *CLOSE* to being really good. Basically, you can compare this to designing a great pet - fluffy, sweet, obedient, smart, quiet, playful - but the thing has 0 sphincter control. It just ... trails poop everywhere across the house, on your furniture, in its bed - that one "little detail" makes it completely non-viable as a pet. Well, same idea here. Game WOULD be good. It's just not.

The available synergies are often neither deep nor engaging enough. This critically affects the game's replayability, providing no incentive to try new, interesting strategies.

I'm really sad about posting a negative review... This is one of the most appealing games I've ever played, but the execution is very poor. The stats on your units do not indicate the actual strentgh of a unit. They are actually coefficients applied to the true hidden stats of each unit. So there's litterally no way in game to know what you're actually playing with. That has to be one of the worst design decisions i've seen in auto battlers, if not the worst. Second pain point : the balance is completely off. Some things are op, some strategies are not working just because ... too weak, even though it shouldn't. I strongly encourage the devs to play their own games more, and have actual stats on the performance of each troop. I'll be more than willing to turn this into a positive review later when the game gets updated, but for now it's barely playable for more than two hours. After that, the frustration of actually not knowing the stats of your units and losing even though your comp makes perfect sense / got lucky with the rolls is just too much to deal with. TLDR : wait for balance and QoL updates, for now not worth it. Wishlist it and keep an eye on it, tho. EDIT : (13th of October 2025) : The compendium has been added, and we know have access to the formulas for stats... but we still don't have easily accessible final numbers for attack and HP. I can see goodwill from the devs to fix the issue, but they keep going around a solution that would be so easy to implement : just give us the final attack and hp of units, as well as their abilities / properties (such as shown in the compendium) on the tooltip when we mouseover a unit. I don't want to have to open an extra menu, then make the calculation for attack and hp myself given in the compendium each time i want an information on a unit. And if you think it's no big deal, keep this in mind : you'll have to do the math yourself every single time you want to check a troop's stats if that that troop has more than one unit in it. There's a good reason why in pretty much all other games the final result of the dev's formula for a stat is clearly shown, instead of giving us the formula. Like I'm sorry, but it really feels like on this specific issue, Knightica is years behind every single other game on the market right now. I can not think of another autobattler with such convoluted way of telling the player what a unit does.

TL;DR: The game has been released but should be an Early Access for a few more months. In principle, it's fun, and the first few games are entertaining as you discover the game, but you quickly realise that it lacks depth and balance. There are no strategic or tactical choices to be made; it's just a mathematical problem: having more stats than your opponent. So you just rely on chance to find the most effective units, given that the majority are useless. It needs more quality of life improvements, other features such as improvements to the economy and the shop to provide strategic choices, choices to make when a unit levels up, multiple paths that give different rewards, the addition of risk-reward mechanics, greater importance given to unit placement, and a complete rebalancing... that kind of things. I cannot recommend the game as it stands.
